items.title: Backend Architecture & High Concurrency
items.description: Microservice architecture for a gaming and live-streaming platform: each game format split into API, Socket, business service, and async consumer, scaling independently by load and carrying peak-hour draw traffic of a thousand bets/orders per second. Kafka for cross-service event streams, Redis and Bull Queue for caching and async settlement, Socket.IO for live rounds.

items.title: Performance Tuning & Refactoring
items.description: Measures before tuning. Replaced runtime JSON parsing with virtual generated columns and composite indexes, taking the query from 5s to milliseconds; separately traced a connection-count alert to pinned connections left by frozen Lambda containers, cutting peak connections by 24% after reworking reclaim.

items.title: Node.js / React.js
items.description: Node.js / NestJS on the backend, React / Next.js (App Router) on the frontend, TypeScript across both — delivering independently from database and API through to the interface. Frontend performance sits in the same scope: first paint, code splitting, caching. Mobile experience includes Flutter.

items.title: Self-Built RAG and Evaluation Framework
items.description: Built a RAG framework from scratch in Python (FastAPI), no LangChain: hybrid retrieval with RRF fusion, LLM reranking, two-tier caching, circuit breakers and provider failover. Evaluation uses a golden dataset and LLM-as-a-Judge, with Recall, MRR, and Groundedness running in CI.

items.title: Commercializing AI Features
items.description: Treats LLMs as revenue-bearing features, not demos: four Claude features shipped as paid subscription content, designed with cost guardrails, graceful degradation, and content moderation, plus a team AI development standard (versioned prompts, AI never blocking payments or matching).

items.title: Team Leadership & Development Standards
items.description: Leading 11 engineers shifted the focus from writing code to building repeatable standards: design review to settle architecture before work starts, code review to hold implementation quality, a release checklist turning deployment risk into process, and documented troubleshooting so problem isolation no longer depends on specific people.
